15-040.r: IDA (World Bank affiliate, set up 24 September 1960) → zero/low-interest loans ('credits') and grants to the world's poorest countries for poverty reduction.
15-040.t: Don't confuse IDA with IFC or MIGA, the other World Bank affiliates in the options; IMF is a separate body.

15-041.r: IMF lends only to member countries; its main function → help members solve balance of payments problems and keep the international monetary system stable.

15-044.r: IMF loans → to meet temporary balance of payments deficits of member countries; IMF is not a development bank (not for projects, gold reserves or capital formation).

15-045.r: Bretton Woods Conference (44 nations, 1-22 July 1944, New Hampshire, USA) → created IMF and IBRD (World Bank) only; not the UN or WTO.
15-045.h: Bretton Woods twins = IMF + World Bank.

15-047.r: United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, 1944 = Bretton Woods Conference → set up IMF and IBRD; GATT was signed separately in Geneva by 23 nations, 30 October 1947.
15-047.c: Answer not printed (*): the question wrongly says GATT was set up at this conference; intended answer is (b) Bretton Woods Conference.

15-048.r: IMF → formally established under the Bretton Woods Agreement on 27 December 1945.
15-048.t: Don't fall for look-alike names such as 'Bretton Stone' or 'S. Woods' Agreement.

15-049.r: IMF has 190 member countries; Andorra became the 190th member in October 2020.

15-050.r: India → founding member of IMF and World Bank; became a member of both on 27 December 1945.

15-052.r: India in IMF (as on June 2024) → 2.75% of SDR quota and 2.63% of votes.
15-052.t: Don't swap the two: quota share (2.75%) is higher than vote share (2.63%).

15-053.r: Gold Tranche (Reserve Tranche) → IMF credit to members; an unconditional drawing right on the IMF, usable any time without conditions or fee; normally 25% of quota.

15-054.r: Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI) and Rapid Credit Facility (RCF) → IMF lending windows for member countries with an urgent balance of payments need.

15-055.r: 'Paper gold' → Special Drawing Rights (SDR) of IMF: an international reserve asset and IMF's unit of account, added to members' foreign currency and gold reserves.

15-057.r: Chinese renminbi (yuan) added to IMF's SDR basket (decided November 2015, effective October 1, 2016), joining US dollar, euro, Japanese yen and pound sterling.

15-058.r: World Economic Outlook → IMF; Human Development Report → UNDP; World Development Report → World Bank; Global Competitiveness Report → World Economic Forum.
15-058.t: Don't link 'World Economic Outlook' to the World Economic Forum just because of the name.

15-059.r: Global Financial Stability Report → IMF, released twice a year (April and October); assesses the global financial system and markets.

15-060.r: Gita Gopinath (Harvard) → IMF Economic Counsellor and Research Director (Chief Economist), appointed October 2018; First Deputy Managing Director since 21 January 2022.

15-061.r: WTO → main security guard of international trade; started 1 January 1995 under Marrakesh Agreement (signed 15 April 1994), replacing GATT, its earlier form.

15-065.r: 3rd WTO Ministerial Conference, Seattle (USA), 30 November-3 December 1999 → failed over linking trade with labour standards and environment issues.

15-066.r: 1st WTO Ministerial Conference, Singapore, 9-13 December 1996 → agreement on expanding world trade in information technology products.

15-067.r: Doha (Qatar) → 4th WTO Ministerial Conference, November 2001, launched Doha Development Agenda; 12th MC Geneva June 2022; 13th MC Abu Dhabi 2024.

15-068.r: WTO uses food safety standards of the Codex Alimentarius Commission (set up 1963 by FAO and WHO) as reference point in dispute settlement.

15-069.r: WTO aims → free trade and resource flows, protection of intellectual property rights, balanced trade, East Bloc-West trade; started 1 January 1995.

15-071.r: Roberto Azevedo (Brazil) → 6th WTO Director-General, replaced Pascal Lamy on 1 September 2013; Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria) → seventh DG from 1 March 2021.
15-071.t: WTO's head is the Director-General, not a 'President' as the question says.

15-072.r: India → WTO member since 1 January 1995 (founding); GATT member since 8 July 1948; WTO has 164 members (Afghanistan 164th, 29 July 2016).

15-074.r: Serbia is not a WTO member; it only has observer status (Slovenia, Slovakia and Colombia are members).

15-075.r: WTO: set up 1 January 1995, born of the Uruguay Round (1986-93) of GATT; aims at trade liberalisation but is still far from achieving it (book).

15-076.r: Doha Round (launched at 4th WTO Ministerial, Doha, November 2001) → central issue: agriculture, especially farm subsidies.

15-077.r: WTO Agreement on Agriculture (Uruguay Round, in force 1 January 1995) three pillars → market access, domestic support, export competition; anti-dumping duties are not a pillar.

15-078.r: Blue box → direct payments to farmers under production-limiting programmes (e.g. gap between MSP and market price); WTO subsidy boxes: green, amber, blue.
15-078.h: Traffic lights: green = go (permitted), amber = slow down (reduce), red = stop (no red box in AoA).
15-078.t: India's MSP itself is amber box; NITI Aayog's Price Deficiency Payment (MSP minus market price) would be blue box.

15-080.r: WTO farm subsidy boxes → green, amber and blue only; there is no red box (and no white box) in the Agreement on Agriculture.
15-080.c: Book marks (c) Red box, but its explanation reads '(c) & (d)': white box is also not a WTO box.

15-081.r: Fertilizer input subsidy and cuts in power/irrigation bills → indirect farm subsidies (not direct); WTO does not ban indirect subsidies; book treats all Indian subsidies as indirect.
15-081.c: Explanation itself says India gives some direct subsidy (food subsidy), yet marks 'all subsidies in India are indirect' correct.

15-082.r: Special Safeguard Mechanism (SSM) → WTO tool letting developing countries temporarily raise tariffs on farm imports during import surges or price falls.

15-083.r: Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) clause (GATT/WTO) → a trade concession given to one member must go to all members; means equal treatment, not favouritism.

15-084.r: GATT = General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade; signed 30 October 1947 at Geneva by 23 countries; in force from 1948, office at Geneva.

15-086.r: Dunkel proposal (draft, December 1991, Uruguay Round of GATT) → related to intellectual property rights (TRIPS), plus services (GATS) and investment (TRIMs).

15-087.r: Arthur Dunkel → Director General of GATT (1980-1993); launched the Uruguay Round in September 1986, which led to WTO.

15-088.r: Dunkel draft (book): mandatory for India to accept all proposals; cut farm subsidies; accepted by Parliament; it did not keep the Multi-fibre Agreement (replaced by Agreement on Textiles and Clothing).

15-089.r: Uruguay Round (1986-1993, 8th round, 123 countries) → GATT trade talks that led to creation of WTO.

15-090.r: TRIMs = Trade-Related Investment Measures (WTO, Uruguay Round) → bars investment rules that favour domestic firms; applies only to trade in goods.

15-091.r: TRIMs → quantitative restrictions on imports by foreign investors are prohibited; covers trade in goods only (not services); not concerned with regulating foreign investment itself.

15-092.r: WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement → part of 2013 Bali Ministerial package; India ratified April 2016 (76th member); in force February 2017, not January 2016.

15-093.r: TRIPS covers copyright, trade marks, industrial designs, geographical indications and more; labour standards are not part of TRIPS.

15-094.r: TRIPS protects trade marks, layout-designs of integrated circuits, geographical indications, patents, trade secrets, copyright; plant breeding is not included.

15-095.r: Intangible investments → brand recognition, intellectual property, mailing list of clients (customer lists); inventory is a tangible asset.
15-095.h: If you cannot touch it, it is intangible.

15-096.r: National IPR Policy (May 2016) → reiterates India's commitment to Doha Development Agenda and TRIPS; DIPP is the nodal agency for IPR in India.

15-097.r: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 → enacted to meet WTO obligations under TRIPS.

15-098.r: Trade Mark → individual/company right, can be licensed; GI → community right, cannot be licensed; GIs cover farm goods, handicrafts and manufactured goods too.
15-098.c: Explanation garbles statement 2 (says GI 'is licensed but has to be registered') though answer (b) treats it as correct.

15-099.r: WTO Agreement on Agriculture → developing countries like India also had to cut farm subsidies (export subsidy 24% by value over ten years; total AMS 13.3%).

15-100.r: 'Agreement on Agriculture', 'Agreement on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures' and 'Peace Clause' → all World Trade Organization terms.

15-101.r: WTO is criticised as puppet of MNCs, cutting sovereignty, favouring free trade over quality; but it does settle trade disputes (Dispute Settlement Body).

15-102.r: Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement (BTIA) → India-European Union talks, begun June 2007 in Brussels; stalled since 2013.

15-103.r: G20 → set up 1999 for Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors; raised to Heads of State level after the 2007-08 crisis; digital public infrastructure was India's G20 priority.

15-104.r: G20 members → about 85% of global GDP, more than 75% of global trade (not 50%), about two-thirds of world population.

15-105.r: G20 = 19 countries + EU + African Union; includes Argentina, Mexico, South Africa, Turkey; Malaysia, New Zealand, Iran, Vietnam, Singapore are not members.

15-106.r: G20 → 19 countries + EU + African Union; no permanent headquarters (not London); India is in Group-2 with Russia, South Africa and Turkey.

15-107.r: India held the G20 presidency from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023; hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit for the first time in September 2023.
15-107.c: Answer not printed (*): India withdrew its 2018 bid; no option fits exactly (presidency began December 2022).

15-108.r: First G20 Summit → Washington D.C., 2008 (true); India took G20 presidency from Indonesia, not Australia, on 1 December 2022.

15-109.r: G20 Common Framework (2020) → endorsed by G20 with the Paris Club; supports Low Income Countries with unsustainable debt, beyond the DSSI.

15-110.r: Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) → tax planning by multinationals that shifts profits to low-tax places; context: curbing tax evasion by multinational companies.

15-111.r: NAMA-11 → group of developing countries (India, Brazil, South Africa, Argentina, Egypt etc.) in WTO Non-Agricultural Market Access talks; seeks flexibility in opening industrial goods trade.

15-112.r: Digital Economy Report → UNCTAD; first released September 2019, second in September 2021.

15-113.r: World Economic Forum → founded 1971 by Klaus Schwab as a not-for-profit foundation; headquarters Geneva; known for its annual meeting at the end of January.

15-114.r: WEF Annual Meeting 2016 → Davos-Klosters, Switzerland (January 2016); the 2024 meeting was also at Davos, 15-19 January, motto 'Rebuilding Trust'.

15-115.r: WEF Davos Summit, 23 January 2018 → PM Narendra Modi named climate change, terrorism and protectionism as global challenges (not Cold War).

15-116.r: Global Talent Competitiveness Index 2020 (INSEAD, released at WEF Davos) → Switzerland 1, USA 2 (not 4), Singapore 3, India 72.

15-117.r: Global Competitiveness Report / Global Competitiveness Index → World Economic Forum (yearly till 2020).

15-119.r: WEF Global Gender Gap Index (first 2006) → four sub-indexes: economic participation, educational attainment, political empowerment, health and survival; leisure is not one.

15-120.r: Global Gender Gap Index / Report → World Economic Forum (first 2006); India 127 of 146 (2023), 129 of 146 (2024).

15-122.r: India in WEF Global Gender Gap Index 2020 → 112th of 153; 2023 → 127th and 2024 → 129th of 146 (Iceland top, Sudan last).

15-123.r: First Gender Social Norms Index (GSNI) → UNDP, 5 March 2020; shows how social beliefs block gender equality in politics, work and education.

15-124.r: Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index → World Economic Forum (every two years); from 2021 replaced by Travel and Tourism Development Index.

15-125.r: India → founding member of Asian Development Bank (1966) and Colombo Plan (1951); not a member of APEC or OECD.
15-125.t: Don't assume India is in APEC just because it is an Asia-Pacific country.

15-126.r: ADB's India Resident Mission → New Delhi (opened 1992).

15-127.r: India is a member of all three → AIIB (founding member, second-largest vote; HQ Beijing), MTCR (2016) and SCO (2017).

15-128.r: European Economic Community → created by Treaty of Rome, 1957; headquarters Brussels; became the European Community within the EU in 1993.

15-129.r: EU: earlier European Community; Single European Act (1986) and Maastricht Treaty were milestones; citizens have dual citizenship; Switzerland is not an EU member.

15-130.r: Poland joined the EU only in 2004 (not a member in 1997); EU now has 27 members incl. France, Germany, Italy, Poland; UK left 31 January 2020.
15-130.c: Answer not printed (*): in 1997 the answer was (d) Poland; today all four options are EU members.

15-131.r: European Stability Mechanism (2012, Luxembourg) → EU agency giving financial help to eurozone countries in distress; successor of European Financial Stability Facility.

15-132.r: EU Stability and Growth Pact (1997) → limits budget deficit to 3% and debt to 60% of GDP; nothing about sharing infrastructure or technology.

15-133.r: Digital Single Market Strategy → European Union (announced May 2015 by Juncker Commission); covers digital marketing, e-commerce and telecom.

15-134.r: EU-US Trade and Technology Council → launched June 15, 2021 in Brussels to coordinate trade and technology issues; not to control technological progress (Statement-II false).

15-135.r: UNOPS S3i (set up March 2020) → invests in affordable housing, renewable energy and health infrastructure; mass rapid transport is not a focus.

15-136.r: FAO's GIAHS (started 2002) → goal: identify and safeguard eco-friendly traditional farm practices, landscapes, agro-biodiversity and local knowledge; not modern technology or GI status.

15-137.r: 100th ILO Conference (1-17 June 2011) → adopted standards to protect domestic workers; ILO created 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles.

15-138.r: ILO Conventions 138 (Minimum Age) and 182 (Worst Forms of Child Labour) → child labour; India's Cabinet approved ratifying both in March 2017.

15-139.r: USA presses developing countries on ILO labour standards (threat of WTO sanctions) but is itself unconcerned with implementing them → A true, R false.

15-140.r: World Social Protection Report → International Labour Organization (ILO).

15-141.r: World Social Security Report → earlier released by ILO; ILO now releases the World Social Protection Report instead.

15-142.r: Crystal Award → World Economic Forum, given annually to artists and cultural leaders who inspire change.

15-143.r: UNSC = United Nations Security Council → 5 permanent members (China, US, France, Russia, UK) + 10 non-permanent members elected for two years.

15-145.r: WTO → generally forbids quantitative restrictions in trade; IMF → finance to correct balance of payments; SAARC → South Asian cooperation; IDA → soft loans.

15-146.r: IMFC (24 members, meets twice a year) → discusses global economic concerns and advises IMF on the direction of its work; World Bank attends as observer.

15-147.r: Headquarters → UNO New York; WTO Geneva; ILO Geneva; FAO Rome.
15-147.t: Don't swap them: ILO is in Geneva, FAO is in Rome.

15-148.r: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), UN agency fighting hunger → headquarters Rome.

15-149.r: UN members: 191 till 2005; Montenegro 192nd (28 June 2006); South Sudan 193rd (14 July 2011); now 193 member states.
15-149.c: Answer not printed (*): option (d) 191 was right till mid-2006; the count is now 193.

15-150.r: Bank for International Settlements → not related to the UN (coordinates central banks); MIGA, IFC and ICSID are World Bank Group units, part of the UN system.

15-151.r: UNCTAD 'Emerging Economies' → Brazil, Mexico and South Africa (also China, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Russia and others).

15-152.r: First APMCHUD → New Delhi, December 2006, theme 'A vision for sustainable urbanization in the Asia-Pacific by 2020'; biennial, hosted by different countries.

15-153.r: Trans-Pacific Partnership → trade deal of 12 Pacific Rim countries (signed 4 February 2016), not all Rim nations, not maritime security; replaced by CPTPP (TPP-11) after US exit.

15-154.r: Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA, earlier Bangkok Agreement, 1975) → Bangladesh, China, India, South Korea, Lao PDR, Mongolia, Sri Lanka; Myanmar is not a member.

15-155.r: 13th NAM Summit → Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, February 2003; 19th → Kampala, Uganda, January 2024; NAM founded 1961 at Belgrade, now 121 countries.

15-156.r: NAM Coordinating Bureau Ministerial Meeting 2019 → Caracas, Venezuela (20-21 July); 18th NAM Summit → Baku, Azerbaijan, October 2019.

15-157.r: OPEC (founded 14 September 1960, Baghdad; 12 members) → emphasis on both production and prices of petroleum, to stabilise oil markets.

15-158.r: China is not an OPEC member; OPEC (Baghdad 1960, HQ Vienna) has 12 members incl. Algeria, UAE; Indonesia suspended membership on 30 November 2016.
15-158.c: Book prints two answers: (b) China, and (c) Indonesia, which suspended its membership in 2016.

15-159.r: SAARC → 8 South Asian members; founded 8 December 1985 at Dhaka by 7 countries; HQ Kathmandu; Afghanistan joined 2007; Thailand and Cambodia are not members.
15-159.h: MBBS PAIN: Maldives, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Afghanistan, India, Nepal.

15-162.r: Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute (IGMRI) → Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; trains SAARC officials; set up 1958 as Grain Storage Research and Training Centre.

15-163.r: First SAARC summit in India → November 1986; SAARC secretariat Kathmandu; 18th summit Kathmandu 2014; 19th (Islamabad, 2016) was cancelled.
15-163.c: Explanation misprints SAARC's founding (Dhaka, 8 December) as 1986; it was founded a year earlier.

15-164.r: UNICEF, IMF and WHO → global organisations; SAARC → regional body of 8 South Asian countries, so it is the odd one out.

15-165.r: UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) → headquarters New York.

15-166.r: Eleventh BRICS Summit 2019 → Brasilia, Brazil (November); 12th (2020) held by video due to COVID-19; 13th (2021) hosted by India.

15-167.r: First BRIC summit → Yekaterinburg, Russia, 16 June 2009 (not Rio); South Africa joined last, September 2010 → BRIC became BRICS; Canada is not a member.
15-167.t: Since 1 January 2024 Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE have also joined, taking BRICS to 9.
15-167.c: Variant 'South Africa joined BRIC in' has no printed answer: its options lack 2010.

15-172.r: 9th BRICS Summit → Xiamen, China, 2017; 15th → Johannesburg, South Africa, 2023; 16th → Russia, 2024.

15-173.r: New Development Bank (BRICS bank) → agreed at 6th BRICS summit, Fortaleza, July 2014; in force July 2015; HQ Shanghai; set up by BRICS, not APEC.

15-175.r: Term 'BRIC' coined in 2001 by British economist Jim O'Neill (Goldman Sachs) in 'Building Better Global Economic BRICs'; his subject → economics.

15-177.r: K.V. Kamath → first President of New Development Bank (2015); succeeded by Marcos Troyjo (2020) and Dilma Rousseff (March 2023).

15-178.r: BRIC: China's GDP exceeds the combined GDP of Brazil, Russia and India (true); China's population is not more than any two others combined (India + Brazil exceed it).

15-179.r: Highest per capita income among given BRICS nations → China (World Bank, 2022); Russia was highest in 2010; India is near the bottom.
15-179.c: Book updates the answer to China using 2022 data; when asked (2010), Russia had the highest.

15-180.r: India and Pakistan became full SCO members in 2017 at the Astana summit; SCO founded 15 June 2001, Shanghai; Shanghai Five (1996) never included Vietnam.
